frozenR3ReserveRule: a selected organisation that is not ACQUISITION_SUCCESSFUL is replaced by the next unused RESERVE in rank order
every replacement inherits the selection slot and its split
if the reserve is exhausted before 110 successful organisations exist: CORPUS_FREEZE_REFUSED
acquisition stops when 110 successful organisations exist OR the reserve list is exhausted, in which case freeze is refused
a smaller corpus is never accepted after reserve exhaustion

q1q2.q1: at every planning point collect ALL pending obligations, sort ascending by selectionIndex, assign the next unused reserve monotonically to EACH; no omission, no reordering by failure type or split, no yield optimisation, no deferral to preserve a reserve
q1q2.q2: a failed replacement opens a new obligation for the SAME slot; a chain ends only on ACQUISITION_SUCCESSFUL or on reserve exhaustion (CORPUS_FREEZE_REFUSED); no third termination state

ownerInterpretation.interpretation: for the frozen Q1/Q2 planning contract, reserve exhaustion occurs when the current complete set of mandatory replacement obligations cannot be assigned from the remaining frozen reserve suffix. It is not necessary first to consume the final physical reserve if doing so would require omitting another simultaneously mandatory Q1 obligation

plannerProof.contrastQ1Only75: 39 consumed + [75] would be assignable to reserve 39 - the refusal is specifically a complete-current-Q1 capacity failure

whyReserve39IsNotAssignedAlone: Q1 at this planning point is [75,76]. Serving slot 75 with reserve 39 while leaving slot 76 unplanned would intentionally omit an existing mandatory obligation for lack of capacity - a new operator-selected partial-planning rule that does not exist. Its possible outcome is irrelevant: even a success on slot 75 would leave slot 76 unsuccessful with zero reserves and far fewer than 110 successes, so the 110-success target is already unreachable under the frozen reserve schedule
